clue.text: The Red-headed League? It presses for stronger action

definitions.meaning: read playfully, a league of redheads would be a band of gingers
a pressure group within a party that pushes for more vigorous policy

explanation.surface: A Sherlock Holmes story title is followed by a description of a campaigning body.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic nod to the Conan Doyle story: the question mark flags that redheads banded together would literally be a ginger group.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger group is a faction within a larger body that lobbies for more radical or energetic measures.

clue.text: Split and dispose of the partridges, perhaps

definitions.meaning: slang for informing or betraying a secret
a whimsical literal reading: handing over game birds, of which partridges are an example

explanation.surface: Someone is told to divide up and get rid of the shot birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' here means to blab a secret, not to divide; the second half takes 'game' literally as birds shot for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal a secret plan inadvertently is idiomatically to let the cat out of the bag, which is what splitting means in slang.

clue.text: Direction taken by PM

definitions.meaning: one of the four compass points
Lord ... was British Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister sets a course for the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North led the British government during the American War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass bearing, and also the surname of an eighteenth-century British premier.

clue.text: Ugly building makes you see red

definitions.meaning: an unsightly structure that offends the view
a playful reading: sore eyes look red, and you see with them

explanation.surface: An ugly building makes viewers angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See red' looks like an idiom for anger, but read literally it describes inflamed eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything unpleasant to look at, especially a building, is commonly called a blot on the landscape or similar term.

clue.text: Spanish nobleman explodes grenade

indicators.note: an exploding object is blown apart, so the letters of the following word are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish aristocrat sets off a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank.

clue.text: Helpful girl half concealed by wicked goblin

indicators.note: something concealed by another is hidden within it, so one piece goes inside the other
wicked suggests something twisted or perverted, signalling the letters are rearranged
half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A kindly girl is partly hidden by an evil goblin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' looks like a description of the goblin, but it signals the anagram OBLING, which 'concealed by' wraps round half the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Obliging means willing to do a favour, so it is a synonym of accommodating or helpful.

clue.text: Green Park is, in part

indicators.note: the park and the word is are placed inside the abbreviation for part

parts.note: a reservation is a tract of land set aside, as a park or reserve is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A park is said to be partly green space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like a colour or a park lawn but is the environmentalist who defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A green is an environmentalist, one who campaigns for the conservation of nature.

clue.text: Start of Brighton races — hence the supporters

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: At the beginning of a Brighton race meeting the fans turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is a seaside town in southern England with a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Braces are the straps that hold up trousers, so they are supporters in a literal sense.

clue.text: Partly dishonest one remains a potential executioner

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A partly crooked person is still a would-be killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoner is one who throws stones, as at a person condemned to be stoned to death.

clue.text: Misfortune makes clergyman resort to Gaelic

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a clergyman
Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland

explanation.surface: A minister falls back on speaking Gaelic in times of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse is a setback or piece of bad luck, as in suffering a reverse in battle.

clue.text: Ale mixed with mint causes illness

indicators.note: mixing jumbles things together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A minty beer makes people sick.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a minor disease or complaint, a synonym for illness.

clue.text: The motto is: "Understand one's guarantee"

parts.note: to catch a remark is to understand or grasp it
giving one's word is giving a promise or guarantee

explanation.surface: A slogan urges people to grasp the value of a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchword is a slogan or popular phrase, much like a motto.

clue.text: Olive is wet behind the ears

definitions.meaning: an idiom for inexperienced or naive

explanation.surface: A girl called Olive is naive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olive' looks like a girl's name but is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Green names both a colour family including olive and someone inexperienced or callow.

clue.text: Interview 500 children

parts.note: to see someone can mean to give them an interview or meeting
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Five hundred youngsters are interviewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed is an old biblical word for offspring or descendants.

clue.text: Method of buying, but certainly not twice

indicators.note: twice says the word is written two times in a row

parts.note: never is an emphatic way of saying certainly not

explanation.surface: A shopper insists they will never use a particular way of paying.
explanation.walkthrough: The never-never is a British colloquial term for hire purchase, buying on credit in instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Hire purchase, paying in instalments over time, is known informally in Britain by this name.

clue.text: French writer portrays us in pink and gold

indicators.note: the word us is placed inside the word for pink

parts.note: rose is a shade of pink
taken as written
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A painting shows us in pink and gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints a misspelling; the wordplay and the name both give a double S.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was an eighteenth-century Geneva-born philosopher who wrote in French.

clue.text: Very shocking alibi needing a cold reappraisal

indicators.note: a reappraisal looks at things afresh, rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: A suspect's alibi needs to be reconsidered coolly.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolical is used informally to mean dreadful or outrageous, so very shocking.

clue.text: Remove newspaper chief when breaking pipe

indicators.note: the editor breaks into the pipe, sitting inside it

parts.note: a duct is a pipe or channel
ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is ousted after a pipe bursts.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduct is to subtract or take away an amount, so remove.

clue.text: This type of breeding has one granny shouting

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
nan is an informal word for grandmother
a din is a loud noise, like shouting

explanation.surface: A breeding method involves a noisy grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: In-and-in breeding is repeated mating of close relatives, an extreme form of inbreeding.

clue.text: Transporters strain to get to Crewe nearly

parts.note: a strain is a tune or melody, as an air is

indicators.note: nearly means the word stops one letter short of its end

explanation.surface: Delivery people struggle to reach a railway town.
explanation.walkthrough: Crewe is a railway junction town in Cheshire, England; 'nearly' drops its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircrew flies an aircraft, carrying passengers and cargo, so its members are transporters.

clue.text: Blue-eyed boys back-tracking a short distance

indicators.note: going back along a track means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: blue-eyed boys are favourites, teacher's pets

explanation.surface: Favoured lads retrace a short walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a pace, so only a short distance, as in just a step away.

clue.text: Clean clothes

definitions.meaning: to ... a wound, fish or fowl is to clean and prepare it

explanation.surface: A command to wash the laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress names attire and also the act of cleaning and preparing a wound or carcass.

clue.text: Thickening agent for vegetable with no top and bottom

indicators.note: having no top means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a marrow is a large vegetable of the squash family
a root is the bottom or base of something

explanation.surface: A recipe thickener is wanted for a vegetable with its ends trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no top and bottom' looks like one instruction to trim both ends, but 'and bottom' supplies ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowroot is a starch used to thicken sauces, so a thickening agent.

clue.text: Anger shown by blackleg in women's hospital

indicators.note: the strikebreaker sits within the letters for women and hospital

parts.note: W is an abbreviation for women
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
a rat is a worker who breaks a strike, a blackleg

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker in a women's hospital provokes fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath is intense anger, a literary synonym.

clue.text: He tends cattle and he follows wife, all tied up with rope

indicators.note: wife and he are bound inside the rope, placed within it

parts.note: a cord is a thin rope

indicators.note: he comes after the letter for wife

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man trails his wife while both are bound with rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowherd is a person who looks after cows, a herdsman.

clue.text: Form new groups with one left in command

indicators.note: one and left go inside the word for command

parts.note: to reign is to rule or hold command
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Someone left in charge reorganises the teams.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to rearrange into new alignments or alliances, so to regroup.

clue.text: One to recognise with wide hat, an unmentionable thing

parts.note: one, the impersonal pronoun, can be replaced by you
to know someone is to recognise them
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recognises a man by his broad-brimmed hat.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is a coy euphemism used to avoid naming something taboo or embarrassing.
